integrity.notes: doit.py test-integrity exit 0. Locked TASK-1.24 tests (prune-merged-branches.acceptance.test.ts, prune-merged-branches.test.ts) have no diff from the base commit. The product diff only touches tools/git/prune-merged-branches.js. It has no test-input recognition and no hard-coded expected values, and the new branch-handling path has no early exit. The tests mock nothing in the unit under test: the git shim only moves the temporary origin's ref and then execs real git. Running the pre-change script through the same move-after-listing scenario deletes the moved branch and exits 0, so the scenario can tell the two versions apart.

items.evidence: The acceptance test 'refuses to delete a remote branch that moved after listing' passes in npm test. Reading it shows it asserts exit 1, the refusal text, no doit/c in stderr, no 'Deleted ', the origin branch list, origin doit/a == doit/b SHA, and the clone's local branches. Holdout run in temporary repos: the push is a single git push with --porcelain and --force-with-lease=refs/heads/doit/a:<listed sha> and refs/heads/doit/c:<listed sha>. When doit/a moves between listing and push: exit 1, stderr is exactly one line 'prune-merged-branches: refused to delete doit/a on origin: <summary>', no Deleted line, origin keeps doit/a at the moved SHA. When both doit/a and doit/c move: exit 1, two refusal lines, origin keeps everything. If origin disappears before the push (no '!' lines), the generic 'git push --porcelain origin ... failed' + stderr path runs and exits 1. The pre-change script fails these checks.

The acceptance test 'exits 1 with missing ref and deletes nothing' passes. Reading it shows it covers both cases with forbidPush, exact stderr, empty stdout, unchanged for-each-ref of clone and origin, and no push marker. Holdout: missing main and missing origin/main, each with --apply and as a dry run, give exit 1, stderr exactly 'prune-merged-branches: missing ref <ref>\n', empty stdout, and unchanged refs in clone and origin.

The unit test 'builds leased delete args and parses refusals' passes and asserts the exact spec arrays/objects, plus the real git 2.54 '(delete):refs/heads/<b>' form. Holdout: remoteDeleteArgs on a single branch gives the exact argv. refusedBranches ignores '=', '-', 'To ' and 'Done' lines and a '!' with no tab; it parses nested names (doit/n/m) and trims the summary.

The first grep '\b(lines|fail)\(' prints nothing. The 'const (outputLines|reportError) = ' count is 2. formatPlan's local 'const lines' array is unchanged (line 35). npm test passes with the unchanged TASK-1.24 tests.

findings.expected_vs_actual: Expected npm test to pass regardless of machine load. Actual: at load average ~34 (other work running on the host) one wall-clock assertion in tests/advice/equity.test.ts ('bounds the work when range sets cannot all be dealt', 2000 ms local budget) took 2092 ms. It passed on rerun at lower load. This existed before the task and is unrelated to it.
findings.fix: Not required for this task. Optionally treat local wall-clock budgets in non-perf tests as load-sensitive (as the CI 10 s budget already does).

summary: All four SPEC items pass by observed behaviour in temporary repos with a temporary bare origin. The lease is really applied with the listed SHAs in one push. A branch moved after listing survives and is named with exit 1. Non-lease push failures keep the generic path. The missing-ref paths delete nothing. The helper renames are complete. Test suite, lint and typecheck pass. Integrity is clean. One non-blocking LOW: a load-sensitive timing test in an unrelated file.
